chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from the one who narrated it, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'A man goes out, then returns to us having acquired much wealth, and we do not know if he earned it from what is permissible or forbidden.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If that is the case, then look at in what manner he spends his wealth. If he spends on what is not appropriate, from what he is sinful for, then it is forbidden.'
ai.seo_question: How to determine if unknown wealth is halal or haram based on spending habits?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'Zann al-Ghalib' (presumption of majority) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing believers to infer the purity of unknown wealth based on observable spending habits. It highlights the practical application of distinguishing between halal and haram in daily transactions, emphasizing that consistent expenditure on valid causes serves as a strong indicator of the wealth's origin.
